references.text: Moses' mother placed him in a 'tebah' (ark/chest) made of reeds and sealed it with pitch, using the same Hebrew word as Noah's ark and describing similar waterproofing – a clear parallel to the ark in Genesis 6:14.
By faith Noah built an ark to save his family, demonstrating his righteousness and obedience to God, serving as an example of faith for followers.
Peter refers to Noah's ark as a foreshadowing of baptism, which now saves believers, drawing a parallel between the water of the flood and the water of baptism.
Noah did everything exactly as God had commanded him, demonstrating his obedience to God's instructions regarding the construction of the ark.
Peter describes Noah as a preacher of righteousness and notes that God preserved him along with seven others when He brought the flood upon the ungodly, highlighting the ark's saving function.
God commands Noah to enter the ark with his entire family, fulfilling the purpose of building the ark described in 6:14.
